subject: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed network — Sentinel Health
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@sentinelhealth.com>, Sentinel Health Legal <legal@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed network — Sentinel Health

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're preparing to move the Redwood Private deployment into our primary VPC (customer-controlled). Before we go live we'd like to document an explicit SLA exception so expectations are aligned. Specifically:

- Sentinel Health will manage the VPC networking, peering, and on-prem VPNs. Any latency or downtime attributable solely to our network (routing, firewall, ISP outages, peering flaps) should be excluded from Redwood uptime/latency SLOs.
- We understand Redwood will remain responsible for the inference runtime, model availability, and any platform-side incidents.
- We can provide network monitoring feeds (NetFlow, BGP logs, and CloudWatch metrics) if Redwood needs visibility for triage.

Attached is our network topology diagram and a short maintenance window schedule.

Can Redwood provide proposed amendment language or a short carveout clause that our legal team can review? Also share any monitoring formats you prefer.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Sentinel Health

Attachments: network-topology-diagram.png (image), maintenance-schedule.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed network — Sentinel Health

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the clear note and attachment. You folks already have the right instincts: Redwood's platform commitments target the inference runtime and control plane we operate; we typically carve out customer-controlled networking. To move forward quickly, can you confirm the following so our legal/ops teams can draft precise amendment text: 

1) Are the VPCs single-AZ or multi-AZ across your account/regions?
2) Do you plan to route traffic across public internet gateways or use direct-connect style circuits?
3) Can you grant a read-only metrics feed (CloudWatch or Prometheus endpoint) and a network incident contact?

Operationally, Redwood can accept an exclusion for "network-originating latency and availability" provided: 
- Sentinel owns and documents scheduled maintenance windows and announces them with >=48h notice for planned work;
- Sentinel provides retention of network logs for at least 30 days for post-incident analysis;
- Redwood retains the right to classify incidents as platform vs network after triage; platform incidents remain eligible for credits under the standard SLA.

I'll loop legal (Priyom) and CS (Grace) to draft amendment language. If you can also share the last 6 months of end-to-end request latency graphs (p95/p99) that will help us scope rollout.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment note: saw network-topology-diagram.png — thanks.

From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@sentinelhealth.com>, Sentinel Health Legal <legal@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed network — Sentinel Health

Alex / team —

Forwarding a quick playbook we agreed internally with ops. Key points:
- We plan multi-AZ VPCs in us-west-2 with redundant VPN concentrators (primary + warm standby).
- Expected maintenance windows: Tue/Thu 02:00-04:00 PT monthly (low traffic), and ad-hoc emergency ops with 6h notice where possible.
- In case of ISP-level incidents (peering or upstream provider), we will attempt automatic failover but cannot guarantee sub-500ms recovery for all traffic classes.

We've attached a matrix that maps types of network incidents to expected mitigation timelines. We understand Redwood will remain responsible for your software stack; for anything that is strictly due to our network we ask that Redwood's SLA credits do not apply. If there are mixed-cause incidents we propose a joint incident review to apportion impact.

Marcus
Senior Network Engineer
Sentinel Health

Attachments: network-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), maintenance-schedule.pdf (pdf)

Date: 2027-01-15T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: SLA carveout for customer-managed network — Sentinel Health

Priyom / Grace —

Looping you in. High level: Sentinel is asking for an explicit carveout where any outage/latency caused purely by their VPC/networking is excluded from Redwood SLA credits. They are multi-AZ and plan redundant circuits but accept some failure modes. They can supply CloudWatch/Netflow and have defined maintenance windows.

Suggested negotiation position (short bullets for legal):
- Redwood will exclude "Customer-controlled network events" from SLA uptime calculations when the root cause is documented in the customer's network logs and confirmed by mutual post-incident review.
- For mixed-cause incidents (both platform and network contributions), a joint incident review will determine the portion attributable to Redwood; credits will be applied proportionally to that portion.
- Customer must provide: 1) network logs covering the incident window, and 2) an agreed contact channel and SLAs for notification of planned maintenance (>=48h).
- Redwood retains the right to require routing tests or packet captures as part of triage; refusal to provide data may forfeit the carveout for that incident.

Risks to call out: enforcement overhead for mixed incidents, potential for slower resolution if log sharing is delayed, and legal pushback on the proportional credit model.

If you (Priyom) can draft a short amendment we can send to Sentinel legal. Grace, please note CS might need to add a telemetry ingestion checklist for Sentinel's ops team.

Thanks,
Alex

Date: 2027-01-18T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood Amendment proposal — Customer Network Carveout (RDWD-4672)

Olivia —

Thanks for the details and attachments. Attached is a concise amendment we propose to add to the Master Services Agreement (excerpt below). If this aligns with Sentinel's expectations, we can route this through DocuSign for countersignature.

Proposed clause (excerpt):
"Customer Network Carveout: Notwithstanding any SLA provisions to the contrary, Redwood's uptime and latency Service Level Objectives shall exclude periods during which the unavailability or increased latency of the Service is caused solely by the Customer's networking infrastructure (\"Customer Network Events\"). Customer shall (a) provide Redwood with network logs and metrics covering the incident window within 5 business days of request; (b) publish planned maintenance windows with at least 48 hours' notice; and (c) participate in a joint incident review for any Customer Network Event claimed to have impacted the Service. In cases where both Redwood and Customer factors materially contribute to an incident, the parties shall conduct a joint incident analysis and apportion any Service Credit based on the portion of impact attributable to Redwood. Failure to provide required network telemetry or to participate in the joint incident review shall void the carveout for that incident."
Operational asks:
- Please share CloudWatch/Prometheus endpoint and a read-only IAM role or similar access for telemetry export.
- Confirm acceptance of 48h maintenance notice and 30-day log retention.

Once we have your confirmation, we'll create a DocuSign envelope (link below) for signatures and include a short annex describing telemetry formats.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/RDWD-4672
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4672

Regards,
Priyom Das

Redwood Inference
